title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving nutrition care services for the drought affected communities in Kahda district, Banadir Region, Somalia.

description.narrative:
ltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtThe project aims to provide curative and preventive life-saving basic health services to IDPs and host communities in Kahda district, Banadir region. An estimated 1382 children aged 6-59 months (704 boys and 677 girls) and 7200 pregnant and lactating women will be targeted for treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition over a 12-month period. This will be achieved through the integration of nutrition services into three existing health facilities and the establishment and operation of four mobile outreach teams. WARDI, in consultation with the target communities, the FMOH Nutrition Section and the BRA, will initiate the project, followed by the recruitment of project staff, including community health workers, ensuring that key parameters such as gender, clan dynamics, minority and marginalized clans and inclusion of PWD are addressed. Once the project is up and running, routine and mass screening of children and PLW for acute malnutrition through MUAC and oedema checks will be carried out to identify and classify children and pregnant and lactating women into different forms of acute malnutrition and link them to appropriate programmes. WARDI operates well-funded primary health centers that also provide TSFP and MCHN, which this project will fully integrate to ensure that children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women receive holistic nutritional support.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size:12.0pt font-family:"gt The project will also promote family led MUAC through orientations and community education to help families identify malnourished children early enough to take appropriate action. At the same time, SAM cases without medical complications will be included in the OTP programme, while SAM with medical complications will be referred to the WARDI-managed stabilization center at Hamarjajab Referral Health Centre or Banadir Hospital for in-patient treatment. Children with moderate acute malnutrition will be referred to the WARDI-managed TSFP programs under the same target facilities. The project will also scale up the promotion of maternal, infant and young child nutrition through preventive services (IYCF counselling, vitamin A supplementation, micronutrient supplementation, deworming, promotion of nutrient-rich complementary foods) at health facilities and through community-based approaches. Mothers' support groups will be established and will be a key component in improving child nutrition and thus reducing the high mortality in the camps. Using its technical support to the MOH on national cold chain management, WARDI will ensure that all sites, including mobile units, provide routine immunization, while identifying and referring children with serious illnesses. A team of CHWs will be identified and trained to be responsible for community mobilization, MUAC screening, tracking of defaults for both nutrition and EPI, and case referral.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
lt/pgtltp style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto text-align:justifyline-height:normal" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-size:12.0pt font-family:"gtltbrgt WARDI will work closely with other stakeholders including the MOH, Banadir Regional Authority and clusters to ensure that the project is implemented as designed and that the target communities are reached. We will create synergies between this project and other projects implemented by WARDI, in particular a WASH project providing clean water to over 30,000 HHs in Kaxda.lt/spangtltspan style="font-size:12.0ptfont-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
